descs.t: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate over her party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, days before the vote. Stevens, who took 47.55% in the Democratic primary, appeared with Rogers at a Detroit church. We walk through what she said, how Democrats reacted and what it could mean on Tuesday.

Haley Stevens, the pro-Israel Democrat who lost the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, is now backing Republican Mike Rogers, saying we can't stand with hate. Hakeem Jeffries and Ayanna Pressley have lined up behind El-Sayed, while President Trump says he would love to have her. We break down why she crossed over and whether it moves the race.

A Democrat who took nearly half the primary vote in Michigan just stood beside the Republican and told voters to back him. Haley Stevens says she cannot stand with hate; her own party calls it betrayal. We look at the fight inside the Democratic Party and what it means for the Senate on Tuesday.

intro.plain: Big news out of Michigan. Haley Stevens, the Democrat who lost the Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers, and she did it standing next to him at a Detroit church. The vote is Tuesday. Her party is furious and Trump says he would love to have her. So chat, does this move votes in Michigan, or is it noise?
intro.mid: Three days before Michigan votes, the Democrat who almost won the Senate primary just endorsed the Republican. Haley Stevens says she can't stand with hate and is backing Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed. Democrats are lining up to call it betrayal, Trump is inviting her into the GOP. Chat, was she right to cross over, or did she just burn her career?
intro.bold: Haley Stevens walked into a Detroit church this morning next to Mike Rogers and told Michigan to vote Republican. A Democrat who took 47.55% in her own party's primary. She says she can't stand with hate. Her party says traitor. Trump says welcome. Chat, one question: if you were a Michigan Democrat, would her endorsement change your vote on Tuesday?
